run_metadata.coverage_summary: WebSearch-only discovery run under the same persistent hard egress block as prior runs: all direct HTTPS to buyer tender hosts is denied by the session network policy (WebFetch to www.tenders.gov.au returned DNS ENOTFOUND again this run), so no buyer-originated detail page, RSS/JSON feed, API or tender document could be opened and every captured tender is therefore headline-level only. Tier 1 was swept via WebSearch snapshots across AusTender/DFAT, buy.nsw, QTenders, Buying for Victoria, Tenders WA, Tenders SA, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL and ACT Tenders; the NT QTOL (tendersonline.nt.gov.au) current list returned the richest live detail this run. Tier 2 (universities, hospitals, water corporations, airports) and Tier 3 (SAP Business Network / Ariba Discovery, South32, Mineral Resources, Chevron, Perth/Sydney airports) were sampled. Three currently-open, buyer-corroborated opportunities carried forward from recent runs were re-confirmed open: the DFAT PNG Health Program ENABLE managing-contractor tender (closing 1 Dec 2026, re-confirmed Open on DevelopmentAid updated ~7 days ago and on DFAT's own notice), the WA EOI for additional trade capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty (closing 23 Dec 2026), and the NT fire-detection-systems maintenance tender (now matched to tender number CIDC020-26, closing 3 Dec 2026). Five further opportunities were newly captured this run from buyer-originated portals: four NT Government tenders surfaced directly from the NT QTOL current list (AGC26-0118 professional advisory services closing 16 Dec; T26-1062 lift repairs/maintenance closing 10 Dec; an aerial photography & LiDAR supply tender and a vehicle rental tender both closing 8 Dec) and one Commonwealth Department of Defence tender (Deep Space Advanced Radar Capability — Alternate Energy Solution managing contractor) which has an official AusTender ATM record. Note: AGC26-0118 was excluded last run as uncorroborated; this run it appeared directly in the NT QTOL current-tender listing with full title, buyer and closing time, so it is now captured. One genuinely new buyer-side platform was found: Unimarket (source-to-pay platform, now parent company of VendorPanel). Tier 3 SAP Ariba Discovery was queried as mandatory but remains login-gated with no publicly visible Australian RFx; the portal is recorded in discovered_sources and no corporate tender was fabricated.
gaps: HARD EGRESS BLOCK (unchanged, re-tested this run): all direct HTTPS to buyer tender hosts is denied by the session network policy. WebFetch to www.tenders.gov.au returned getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND this run, matching prior runs, so no buyer-originated detail page, RSS/JSON feed, API or tender document could be opened. Every tender in this run is therefore headline-level only and could not be verified against its live portal detail page or documents; deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, contacts and most commercial fields are null. To restore full discovery and deliverables extraction, the Tier 1/2/3 tender hosts need to be allowed in the session's network settings.

Tier 1: AusTender, buy.nsw Opportunities Hub, QTenders/Queensland Procurement Solution, Buying for Victoria, Tenders WA, Tenders SA and Tenders ACT could only be read through cached WebSearch snapshots (several of which were stale, e.g. the Buying for Victoria 'open' snapshot still listed October 2026 closing dates). Current open-tender lists filtered by publish/closing date could not be retrieved, so newly-published (last 24-48h) listings on those portals are very likely under-captured. The NT QTOL portal was the exception and returned usable current detail.

Tier 3 (SAP Business Network Discovery / SAP Ariba Discovery): queried as mandatory, but the public posting board requires a free supplier login to view open Australian RFx; no authenticated session is available, so no individual corporate opportunity was publicly visible. Portal recorded in discovered_sources (access_method=portal-registration); no corporate tender fabricated.

Tier 3 corporate sampling returned only aggregator-held or login-gated detail: South32 and Mineral Resources supplier pages (both already known) route tendering through SAP Ariba; Chevron Australia opportunities appear via ICN Gateway and its own apexportal; Perth Airport new-runway packages route through the CPB Contractors procurement portal and ICN Gateway. No publicly-visible corporate RFx could be captured without login.
Tier 3 invitation-only RFx (e.g. management-consultancy RFPs sent directly to shortlisted/panel suppliers) remain out of scope and undiscoverable by design, as noted in the task spec.

Unverified aggregator signal NOT captured as a tender: australiantenders.com.au lists the Defence 'Deep Space Advanced Radar Capability — Alternate Energy Solution' (ID 630837) with an estimated value ~A$80M and a 17 Dec 2026 closing date; the official AusTender ATM record for it exists (captured as a tender here) but could not be opened, so the value and closing date remain unverified and are recorded in notes, not in the value/closing_date fields.
Transurban has no buyer-originated supplier/tender URL confirmable from search this run; not recorded rather than guessing a URL.
Melbourne Airport and Brisbane Airport procurement/supplier portals could not be located via search this run; deferred to a future run.
recommended_seed_additions: Unimarket (unimarket.com) — source-to-pay / e-procurement platform, now the parent company of VendorPanel; used by NSW Department of Education (2,000+ schools), Murdoch Children's Research Institute and (via Local Buy) Queensland councils. Primarily a catalog/purchasing platform rather than a public tender-advertising board, so medium value for open-tender discovery, but worth tracking as the VendorPanel ecosystem consolidates.

Local Buy (localbuy.net.au) — Local Government Association of Queensland's central procurement body operating supplier panels/arrangements for Queensland councils and eligible not-for-profits; a legitimate Tier 2 public-sector buyer channel (surfaced via the Unimarket/VendorPanel search). URL not yet directly verified this run; verify before relying.

Defence DSRG / Estate Works Program tender forecast (defence.gov.au Estate Works Program Tender Forecast PDF) — Defence publishes a forward tender forecast worth monitoring as an early-market-engagement discovery source for Commonwealth estate works.

tenders.title: Managing Contractor — PNG Health Program ENABLE (Enhanced National Advice, Bilateral partnership, and Learning and Evidence)
tenders.buyer: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
tenders.description: DFAT is seeking a managing contractor to implement the PNG Health Program ENABLE, which supports delivery of the PNG–Australia Health Partnership Strategy 2024–2034 by strengthening selected national enabling functions and strategic partnerships that advance integrated primary health care in Papua New Guinea, from 2027 for an initial five-year term.
tenders.scope_of_work: Per the DFAT concept note, the managing contractor would deliver selected national enabling functions and strategic partnerships supporting Australia's broader health portfolio in PNG. Full scope could not be read this run because the tender detail/documents could not be opened.
tenders.submission_method: Via AusTender / as directed in the DFAT business notification
tenders.reasoning: Carried forward from recent runs and re-confirmed open this run via WebSearch: DFAT's own ENABLE business notice plus a DevelopmentAid listing showing Status: Open with a last update ~7 days ago. Buyer-originated source is DFAT's development business-opportunities page; AusTender is the lodgement channel.
tenders.notes: Headline-level only — the AusTender ATM record and tender documents could not be opened this run (egress block), so deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria and contacts remain null. Closing date/time carried from prior-run capture; re-verify against the live AusTender record once portal access is restored.

tenders.title: Expression of Interest — Additional Trade Capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty
tenders.buyer: Government of Western Australia (Ports portfolio / Fremantle Ports)
tenders.description: The WA Government has called for expressions of interest from industry to explore additional trade capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty, a strategically important piece of State port infrastructure that handles fertiliser products and industrial commodity imports. The EOI tests whether the market can finance, build and operate near-term infrastructure to ease capacity constraints at the jetty.
tenders.scope_of_work: Market sounding on options to finance, build and operate near-term infrastructure adding trade capacity at Kwinana Bulk Jetty. Full EOI document could not be opened this run.
tenders.reasoning: Carried forward and re-confirmed this run via the WA Government media statement (released EOI on Tenders WA on 10 Nov 2026). Buyer-originated source is the WA Government; EOI is hosted on Tenders WA, which could not be opened directly.
tenders.notes: Headline-level only. This jetty-capacity EOI is distinct from the separate Westport Kwinana Bulk Terminal Redevelopment marine-infrastructure EOI. Closing date carried from prior capture; verify on Tenders WA when access is restored.

Unimarket is a source-to-pay e-procurement platform and is now the parent company of VendorPanel; its Australian buyers include the NSW Department of Education (2,000+ schools), Murdoch Children's Research Institute, and (via Local Buy) Queensland councils and eligible not-for-profits.

Full opportunity detail is behind buyer-specific registration.
